preamble: Denasalization of nasal [õ] to oral [o]. In Galician-Portuguese, the nasal vowel produced when intervocalic n was lost lost its nasality again in hiatus: Old Galician-Portuguese bõa and pessõa became Portuguese boa and pessoa. In Polish, the nasal back vowel ą [ɔ̃] is pronounced oral [ɔ] before /l/ and /w/.

examples.note: Intervocalic n was lost after nasalizing the vowel before it; the nasal vowel was later denasalized in hiatus. Archaic and dialectal bõa still keeps the nasal.
Before /l/ or /w/ (ł), ą and ę lose nasality and are pronounced oral [ɔ] and [ɛ]. The Polish vowel is open-mid [ɔ̃].

context: Polish: before /l/ or /w/; Galician-Portuguese: in hiatus after loss of intervocalic n
allophones_note: Polish nasal vowel denasalization before sonorants
